status_note: Epoch 3 is running: genesis T 2026-10-13 21:00:00 UTC, four validators and one DHT host. The values below are the ones it runs with.

global_id.note: Signature replay domain (ConfigParam 19), confirmed by the owner (decision D03 in memo public-testnet/README.md): public testnet 2, mainnet 1, local development network 3. No other TOS network and neither TON network (mainnet -239, testnet -3) uses 2.

genesis.schedule_note: Testnet schedule, decided 2026-10-12 after the first epoch: the canonical template's 131,072 s initial set and 65,536 s terms meant no key block, and so no state or consensus-DB GC, for the first 34 h, and the disks filled first. Here the first election opens at T + 4 h and closes at T + 5.5 h, the elected set takes office at T + 6 h, and the set rotates every 4 h, each rotation a key block. testnet_lib.validator_schedule checks the values against each other.
genesis.source_date_epoch_note: Chosen and frozen by the coordinator at the ceremony (decision D03). It must lie in the future when the ceremony runs and leave the initial validator set enough lifetime to complete the first two elections.

features.note: Neither may be activated on the public testnet until its own acceptance gate passes (memo public-testnet/README.md section 3.2).

retention.note: Validator consensus databases are deleted only behind the GC checkpoint, which never passes the last key block, state_ttl or the persistent-state serializer (production/Production-Node.md, 'The GC floor'). With a 4 h term a validator normally keeps under 5 h of them, about 30 GB at the first epoch's 145 GB a day, and up to about 10 h (60 GB) when a key block opens a new 2^17 s persistent-state period and the serializer waits up to 6 h.

validator_logs.note: Owner decision 2026-10-12: at most 2 GB of logs per validator (memo EPOCH-1-FINDINGS.md, E1-05). One file per engine thread (threads + 1 files), each with keep_files rotated copies, plus the session stats file, which the engine rotates at 256 MiB keeping one .old. About an hour of history at the first epoch's volume.

elections.note: What onboard-validator.sh moves for each genesis validator, as run in epoch 1. The bootstrap wallet holds 100,000 TOS: four operators at 20,100 leave 19,600, burned after the second election. Each pool holds two fixed stakes of 10,002 (the Elector subtracts 1 TOS before it compares with the 10,000 minimum), for the first and the overlapping second election.

authorization.refund_target_note: Onboarding funds the first authorization to funds_target (20 TOS, about 4 stakes): the operator wallet keeps only about 75 TOS after onboarding. testnet-elections.py refund renews to refund_target instead: 260 TOS is 60 stakes at about 4.29 TOS, ten days of 4-hour elections, the target the owner approved for epoch 3. The operator wallet needs about 240 TOS more than its reserve first (testnet-elections.py fund).
authorization.operator_reserve_note: What testnet-elections.py refund leaves in the operator wallet at least. The election task sends 20 TOS (POOL_RELAY_BUDGET) with every stake and refuses to stake below 20.2 TOS (that plus WALLET_COMPUTE_FEE, 0.2 TOS), tos tosctl/src/node-control/elections/src/runner.rs send_stake; 30 TOS is that plus a margin. A refund that left 17.77 TOS kept all four validators out of an election.

host_requirements.note: Testnet floors checked by scripts/preflight.py before a host is prepared. Measured on 12 GB / 6-core VMs: a running validator holds about 6 GB RSS, and build-node-binaries.sh peaked at 8.4 GB with 4 jobs (3.2 GB for a DHT build with 2). A 12 GB VM reports about 11.6 GiB MemTotal. Production requirements are production/Hardware-and-Hosting.md, not these.
